verdict.rationale: Name.com's Core API supports headless use without a UI: it uses HTTP Basic auth with API tokens issued for development and production, and offers official TypeScript, Go and PHP SDKs. A sandbox environment is explicitly meant for running automated integration tests without touching real domains or incurring charges. However, there is no documented CI-specific guidance (pipeline setup, secrets handling) and no official CLI, so coverage of 'run in CI' is only implied rather than complete. missing for 10: CI pipeline integration docs or examples, official headless CLI, published OpenAPI spec (probe 404), independent hands-on corroboration of CI automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: The Core API uses **HTTP Basic Authentication** with your name.com API credentials.
Go to Account Settings → Security → API Tokens and issue both development and production tokens
so you can build and run automated integration tests without affecting real domains or incurring real charges
Official client SDKs for the name.com Core API. They give you typed clients that map directly to the API reference
